title: Redwood POC weekly sync - Quantaco AI - cost econ
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics: tokens/sec/$ benchmarking, caching and batching tradeoffs. Reviewed recent 24h run results, identified tuning to improve tokens-per-dollar via cache hit rate and batch sizing, agreed on next steps (stress run, updated quant profiles, pricing sheet).
next_steps: Samir to share updated cost_econ_v3.xlsx and final pricing tiers by 2026-03-27
Riley to run 24h stress run with suggested batch config (batch_size=12, max_latency=180ms) and share logs by 2026-03-30
Omar to provide 3 representative prompt sets for accuracy/eval by 2026-03-28
Ava to schedule follow-up demo with security docs attached by 2026-04-01
action_items: Samir Patel — Share updated cost_econ_v3.xlsx and pricing breakdown — due 2026-03-27
Riley Chen — Run 24h stress benchmark w/ cache warmed, batch=12, quant profile BETA-2 — due 2026-03-30
Omar Aziz — Provide 3 prompt sets + expected quality thresholds — due 2026-03-28
Elena Rodriguez — Confirm legal review window and required SOC2 artifacts — due 2026-03-31
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call... Samir from Redwood, Riley our SE, Ava CSM. Quantaco team?
[00:10] Elena: Hi yep Elena here. Marcus, Priya and Omar are on.
[00:23] Samir: Cool. Today is cost econ focus — tokens per second per dollar, caching savings and batching tradeoffs. We ran that 24-hour benchmark last week, Riley will walk through results.
[00:35] Riley: Ok, quick disclaimer the transcription sheet has a couple typos, but main numbers: baseline hosted run (r4-small) avg throughput 6.4 tokens/sec at median latency 220ms, cost about $0.018 per 1k tokens which maps to roughly 355 tokens/$ for the baseline config.
[01:00] Marcus: Wait, 355 tokens per dollar? That seems low compared to earlier numbers, can you repeat the math?
[01:08] Riley: Sure, so our cost model includes infra + per-request overhead; the dedicated bench using g5x2 equiv shows 1,200 tokens/sec nominal when batching aggressively, which is about 1.3M tokens/hour => ~31M tokens/day. With reserved pricing assumptions in the sheet that gives ~1,100 tokens/$ (approx), but that assumes 65% batch utilization.
[01:35] Priya: Where does cache fit in? Our workload has a lot of repeated prefixes for intent classification.
[01:41] Riley: Good question. We tested with prefix/KV cache warmed vs cold. Warm cache improved tokens/sec effective by ~40% in our sec sample — not linear because latency drops and it reduces decoder load. In numbers: warm cache run showed 1,680 tokens/sec peak (vs 1,200 cold), which bumped tokens per dollar to ~1,540 under same reserved assumptions.
[02:10] Omar: Are those numbers with quantization applied? We saw some quality degradation in BFloat16 to int8 attempts.
[02:18] Riley: The numbers I just quoted were with quant profile BETA-2 (4-bit aware ops, minimal accuracy drop on our eval set). We also ran INT8 aggressive which saved another ~15% cost but dropped rouge/accuracy on some prompt sets beyond your thresholds — we'll share the eval matrix.
[02:40] Elena: Can you call out the quality-vs-cost tradeoff more explicitly? We need to present to product folks.
[02:47] Riley: Sure. Quick table in the sheet:
- No quant + cold cache: ~350 tokens/$ (hosted).
- No quant + warm cache: ~490 tokens/$.
- BETA-2 quant + warm cache: ~1,540 tokens/$.
- INT8 aggressive + warm cache: ~1,770 tokens/$ but with 4-7% drop on entity extraction accuracy for language X in our sample.
[03:25] Marcus: The 4-7% drop is unacceptable for some customers. Do you have per-prompt breakdowns?
[03:31] Riley: We do. Omar, can you upload the three prompt types you mentioned earlier? We'll attach per-prompt accuracy to the sheet.
[03:38] Omar: Yep will do.
[03:40] Samir: Important note — these tokens/$ numbers assume 24/7 utilization. If your traffic is spiky, reserved capacity math changes and burst pricing matters. That's in the assumptions tab.
[03:55] Elena: Right, our traffic is heavy M-F 9–6 and quiet nights. So utilization will be ~42% effective. How does that affect numbers?
[04:03] Riley: With 42% utilization, effective tokens/$ drops roughly 30–40% vs the 65% assumption — so BETA-2 warm-cache would be closer to ~900–1,050 tokens/$. We flagged this in the sheet with an alternate run.
[04:20] Priya: Do we have suggestions to mitigate? Like auto-scaling vs burst pools?
[04:25] Samir: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports burst pools and autoscale. Strategy: reserved for baseline (predictable min), autoscale burst for peaks — and cache to reduce token generation. That way your reserved commit buys more value.
[04:40] Riley: Also tuning batch size matters — we tested batch sizes 4, 8, 12, 20. Throughput increased with batch size but median tail latency rose. For your SLAs (p95 < 400ms) batch=12 looked like best compromise; batch=20 gave 25% more tokens/sec but p95 spiked over 700ms.
[05:10] Elena: So batch 12 with warm cache + BETA-2 quant gives us X tokens/$ but keeps latency within our SLA?
[05:17] Riley: Correct, approximated tokens/$ around 1,200 with your utilization profile.
[05:22] Marcus: Can we quantify cache hit rate improvement required to hit our target of 1,500 tokens/$?
[05:28] Riley: From our modeling, you'd need ~75% prefix hit rate with batch=12 and BETA-2 quant to approach 1,500 tokens/$. Current measured hit rate in the sample dataset was 52%.
[05:40] Omar: We can probably engineer prefix normalization to increase hit rate, may add a small CPU cost but big savings on GPU tokens.
[05:47] Priya: Any reliability concerns with high cache dependency? Like cache eviction and staleness on model updates?
[05:54] Riley: Good point. We recommend versioned caches keyed with model version/kv-hash, and background refresh. Redwood's runtime supports atomic cache invalidation per model rollout so you don't get stale hits after a model swap. We'll share the doc for cache semantics.
[06:12] Elena: Nice. On the security side — we still need SOC2 artifacts and audit logs for Private deployment.
[06:18] Ava: We're preparing SOC2 pack for customers; I'll attach the SOC2 + ISO summary and the audit log export sample.
[06:24] Elena: Great. Next I want to drill into the 24h stress run details — Riley, walk us through anomalies.
[06:30] Riley: Sure. Over 24h we saw three windows of degraded throughput during simulated deploys — those were controlled canary rollouts where cache was partially invalidated. Peak drop was ~18% tokens/sec for ~12 minutes during concurrent rollout + autoscaling event. We have recommendations: stage cache refresh, pre-warm nodes on deploy, and prefer canary rollout to limited traffic slices.
[07:00] Marcus: That explains the occasional errors we saw in the logs. Any recommended SLAs to expect during rollouts?
[07:06] Samir: We aim for graceful degradation — canary + fallback to lower-capacity model variants; with that policy, effective uptime for serving should remain >99.5% even during rollouts. We'll include a sample rollout policy in the deck.
[07:22] Priya: Back to cost math — can you show the per-token breakdown: infra cost, licensing, overhead?
[07:29] Riley: Yep the sheet breaks it down: infra ~65% of unit cost, runtime/ops overhead ~20%, licensing & support ~15% (if enterprise add-ons). There's also cold-start penalty per request that gets amortized with caching.
[07:45] Omar: For evaluation, do you have the raw logs or summaries? Our SRE wants to plug into our observability.
[07:52] Riley: We'll share aggregate logs and the tracing hooks; Redwood supports OTEL exports. We'll send a sample dashboard JSON and the query snippets.
[08:05] Elena: One more on batching: is dynamic batching possible where small requests are prioritized? We can't increase p95 for low-latency interactive flows.
[08:15] Riley: Yes, we support route-level policies: low-latency route with batch cap 4, priority queue, and high-throughput route with batch 12/20. You can route by API key or route name. That lets you preserve interactive p95 while still batching background calls.
[08:32] Marcus: Sounds good. Anything on cost smoothing? We hate monthly spikes.
[08:36] Samir: Consider commitment + burst buffer. Also model caching reduces tokens generated, smoothing costs.
[08:42] Priya: About quantization again — is A/B testing in production safe? We want to run on small % of traffic first.
[08:49] Riley: Absolutely. Redwood supports canary quant rollouts — you can route 5% traffic to quantized variant and compare accuracy and latency. We recommend an initial 1-5% for a week, monitor eval metrics.
[09:05] Elena: Great. Let's recap the spikes in the 24h run and the mitigations you suggested.
[09:12] Riley: Spikes caused by simultaneous rollout + autoscale; mitigations: stage cache invalidation, pre-warm nodes, throttle rollout traffic slice, use fallback model variant.
[09:22] Samir: For next steps: we'll update the cost sheet with your utilization assumptions and share the final pricing tiers; Riley will run the 24h stress test with batch=12 and warmed cache; Omar will provide prompt sets; Ava will send SOC2 docs.
[09:38] Elena: Sounds good. Quick Q: can Redwood provide an estimate for 12-month committed pricing if we sign Dedicated?
[09:44] Samir: Yes, we'll include a committed pricing column in the sheet. Expect incremental discount as commit increases; I'll put rough bands and we can formalize in SOW.
[09:54] Marcus: Also want a side-by-side cost sim vs building in-house with Spot GPU infra.
[09:59] Samir: We can run a comparison — we have a build-vs-buy template. I'll include that.
[10:05] Elena: Ok thanks everyone. We'll look for the sheet and Riley's logs.
[10:10] Samir: Thanks — meeting notes and action items will be in the follow up.
[10:15] (end)
file_notes: Shared artifacts referenced: cost_econ_v3.xlsx (sheet), 24h-benchmark-logs.tar.gz (s3 link), SOC2-summary.pdf. Transcription has occasional name misspellings per Fireflies typical output.
